2010_011_100510regmtg.paragraph: Agenda and meeting packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of October 5, 2010, at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Contents include recognition of National AP Scholars, consent-agenda minutes from September 21 and September 28, 2010, an Anne Mull report on the Common Core Standards, the 2010/2011 Sex Education Advisory Board roster, and a proposal to cancel the November 2, 2010, meeting. The most consequential item is Mark Rajter's legislative update: HB 5872 would restore the ($154) per-pupil cut as a one-time payment worth $2.13 million or $177/pp to Troy, while a higher retirement system employer rate costs approximately $600,000, a ($50) per-pupil decrease, for a net of $127/pp.

**Meeting**
Troy Board of Education regular meeting, October 5, 2010, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (district offices 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000). Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except in July and August, and streamed at www.troy.k12.mi.us/tsdnews/video.htm.

**Recognition**
More than 350 Troy students were honored by the College Board for performance on Advanced Placement exams during the past school year, in four categories: AP Scholar, AP Scholar with Honors, AP Scholar with Distinction, and National AP Scholar. National AP Scholar requires an average grade of four on all AP exams taken and eight or more AP exams during the school year. Juniors receiving the honor and invited to the meeting: Raymond Chen, Mason Liang, and Xiao Zhu.

**Consent agenda**
A. Minutes of the September 21, 2010, Board meeting. B. Minutes of the September 28, 2010, Special Board Workshop. C. Accept a leave request from Judy Hunsberger, Principal, Morse Elementary School.

**September 21, 2010 minutes (highlights)**
Called to order by President Underwood at 7:00 p.m.; Board members Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, and Pochodylo present with Superintendent Fowler, administrators Birmingham, Bryan, Keeling, Machesky, Mull, Rajter, Stromayer and Witt, and approximately 18 additional audience members. Student representatives Bria Ellis (Athens) and Andrew Michail (Troy High, fourth year) were welcomed. Resolution 10-099 approved consent items including the August 2010 Treasurer's Report (7-0). Resolution 10-100 named the Board negotiating teams for the TEA/MEA/NEA contract expiring August 14, 2011, and the TESA/MEA/NEA contract expiring June 30, 2011 (7-0). Anne Mull reported on 2010/2011 professional development, the Kalpa system, and the TransACT translation subscription; approximately 12% of students are English language learners and about 80 languages are represented. Resolution 10-101 certified Ida Edmunds, Paula Fleming, and Nancy Philippart as delegates to the MASB 2010 Delegate Assembly on November 4, 2010. Closed session for negotiations ran 7:15 p.m. to 9:46 p.m.; adjourned 9:47 p.m.

**Curriculum**
A Common Core Standards report by Anne Mull, Director of Instruction and Assessment: standards developed under the National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and the Council of Chief State School Officers, adopted unanimously by Michigan's State Board of Education on June 15, 2010; 48 states, the District of Columbia and two territories supported initial development and 35 states had adopted as of September 1, 2010; new multi-state assessments target Fall 2014. Also a consideration to approve the 2010/2011 Sex Education Advisory Board membership, co-chaired by Larry Hahn and Kevin Wilson.

**Business — Legislative Update (Mark Rajter)**

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| SB 1163 FY 10-11 per pupil decrease | ($154) per student |
| HB 5872 if signed / if allowed to become law | $2.13 million to TSD, $177/pp |
| Veto, 2x-basis formula | Troy = $1.33 million |
| Veto, Title 1 formula | TSD = $141,268 |
| ORS employer rate 10/1/2010 | 19.41% (Pension Plus members 17.91%) |
| ORS rate 11/1/2010–9/30/2011 | 20.66%; Pension Plus 19.16% |
| Increased school employer rate | 1.25%, approximately $600,000, ($50) per pupil |
| FY 10-11 net | $127/pp |

**Other and closed session**
Consideration to cancel the November 2, 2010, Board of Education meeting, and a resolution to enter closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c).

Agenda cover, agenda, and supporting packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of October 5, 2010, convening at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The district masthead lists 4400 LIVERNOIS, TROY, MICHIGAN 48098, 248.823.4000. Board meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except in July and August, and may be viewed online at www.troy.k12.mi.us/tsdnews/video.htm. The agenda order: Pledge of Allegiance; Recognition (Advanced Placement Scholars); Additions and Deletions; Public Communication (agenda items); General Consent Agenda; Personnel; Curriculum; Business; Public Communication (non-agenda items); Other; Closed Session; Adjournment.

RECOGNITION — ADVANCED PLACEMENT HONORS. More than 350 Troy students were honored for performance on Advanced Placement exams during the past school year. The College Board honored Troy students in four award categories: AP Scholar, AP Scholar with Honors, AP Scholar with Distinction, and National AP Scholar. The evening's recognition covered National AP Scholar honorees, an award granted to students who receive an average grade of four on all AP exams taken last year and who also take eight or more AP exams during the school year. A number of those students were seniors last year; the students invited who achieved the honor during their junior year are Raymond Chen, Mason Liang, and Xiao Zhu. Recommended action: distribute certificates.

GENERAL — CONSENT AGENDA. Item A, minutes of the September 21, 2010, Board of Education meeting; item B, minutes of the September 28, 2010, Special Board of Education Workshop; item C, accept a leave request from Judy Hunsberger, Principal, Morse Elementary School. The suggested resolution approves items A, B, and C at one time.

MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 21, 2010 (Services Building). President Underwood called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Ms. Underwood, Board members Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, and Pochodylo were present, along with Superintendent Fowler; administrators Birmingham, Bryan, Keeling, Machesky, Mull, Rajter, Stromayer and Witt; and approximately 18 additional members of the audience. Under Recognition, President Underwood welcomed Bria Ellis, a senior who will represent Athens High School on the Board, and welcomed back for the fourth year Andrew Michail, who will represent Troy High School this semester. There were no additions or deletions and no public communication at that point.

Resolution 10-099, moved by Ms. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Fleming, approved consent agenda items: A, minutes of the September 7, 2010, Board of Education meeting; B, minutes of the September 14, 2010, Board of Education Workshop; C, Treasurer's Report for August 2010. Ayes 7, Nays 0.

Resolution 10-100, moved by Mrs. Edmunds and supported by Mr. Miletti, addressed the Board Negotiating Team. It appoints Rajter, Jan Keeling and Richard Machesky as team members to represent the Board in upcoming negotiations with the TEA/MEA/NEA, whose contract expires on August 14, 2011, with Jasen Witt named chief spokesperson. It further appoints Jasen Witt as chief spokesperson and Mark Rajter, Richard Machesky and Bonnie Lobert as team members for upcoming negotiations with the TESA/MEA/NEA, whose contract expires on June 30, 2011, and states the Board's desire to reach a fair and equitable agreement with each Association. Ayes 7, Nays 0. Mrs. Edmunds commented that she hoped negotiations would begin immediately or very soon so the district would not again be continuing negotiations after the start of the school year.

Under Curriculum, Mrs. Anne Mull, Director of Instruction and Assessment, updated the Board on professional development activities for the 2010/2011 school year, presenting the professional learning opportunities that had occurred and how they would be sustained for teachers and administrators. She explained the Kalpa system and a new online survey and sign-in procedure intended to maintain course quality and ensure effective application to the curriculum, and discussed the district's subscription with TransACT as a communication tool for the multi-cultural community. Mr. Hauff asked when 2011 PD courses would be offered and when survey data would be examined; Mrs. Mull said surveys had already been reviewed and elementary teachers would like a catalog of PD choices. Ms. Philippart asked how many PD hours the state requires to be taken online; Mrs. Mull said five hours are required through virtual learning experiences. Mr. Miletti asked about the Atlas Rubicon system; Mrs. Mull explained Oakland Schools will upload mini lessons to the web that can be shared across the district. Ms. Underwood asked about the percentage of ELL students and the number of languages represented; Mrs. Mull responded that approximately 12% of the student population are English language learners, and Dr. Fowler stated approximately 80 languages are represented in the district. Mrs. Pochodylo asked whether TransACT translations preserve proper context; Mrs. Mull stated TransACT is approved for translation, unlike Google Translate, which has literal-translation challenges.

In public communications, Rhonda Hendrickson addressed the Board urging the district to support Proposal 1 to keep the Troy Public Library open, arguing Troy's educational system should partner with the community to maintain high expectations for youths learning in and outside of school. Business: none.

Resolution 10-101, moved by Mr. Miletti and supported by Mrs. Pochodylo, certified Mrs. Ida Edmunds, Mrs. Paula Fleming, and Ms. Nancy Philippart as delegates to the Michigan Association of School Boards 2010 Delegate Assembly on November 4, 2010. Yes 7, No 0. Student representative Bria Ellis reported that Athens High School's newly renovated media center would open the following Monday with several new computers and three rooms for quiet study; the after-school tutoring program had expanded to all core classes and foreign languages; Athens hosted a Marching Band competition the prior weekend and placed one point away from first place; and the Board was invited to the Ford Drive One Event on October 15 from 3:00 to 7:30 p.m., with proceeds going toward scholarships for Athens students. Andrew Michail spoke about improvement in academics including ACT scores from the previous year, the Homecoming parade and game on Friday, September 24th (Colts vs. West Bloomfield), and the dance on Saturday, September 25th from 7 to 10 p.m.

Resolution 10-102, moved by Mr. Miletti and supported by Mrs. Pochodylo, resolved that as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(h), the Board go into closed session to discuss negotiations. Roll call: Edmunds Yes, Fleming Yes, Hauff Yes, Miletti Yes, Philippart Yes, Pochodylo Yes, Underwood Yes; Ayes 7, Nays 0; motion carried 7-0. The Board moved to closed session at 7:15 p.m. and reconvened at 9:46 p.m. Adjournment was moved by Mr. Miletti and supported by Mrs. Fleming; Yes 7, No 0; the meeting adjourned at 9:47 p.m. Submitted by Nancy L. Philippart, Secretary (NLP/jb).

MINUTES OF THE SEPTEMBER 28, 2010, SPECIAL BOARD WORKSHOP (Services Building). President Underwood called the workshop to order at 6:04 p.m. Present in addition to Ms. Underwood were Mrs. Edmunds, Mr. Hauff, Mrs. Fleming, and Mrs. Pochodylo; Ms. Philippart was absent. Also in attendance were Superintendent Fowler and administrators Birmingham, Keeling, Machesky, Rajter, and Bryan, plus one additional community member. Items discussed: Public Communication; 2004 Bond Update; Cloud Computing; Bus Inventory and Purchase — Status of Current Contract with First Student; Facility Planning; Legislative Update — Teacher/Administrative Performance Evaluations; ARD Update; Other — Library Proposal; Adjournment. The meeting was adjourned at 9:44 p.m. Submitted by Nancy L. Philippart, Secretary (NLP:jb).

CURRICULUM — REPORT: COMMON CORE STANDARDS, presented by Anne Mull. The National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and the Council of Chief State School Officers led development of the Common Core Standards for grades K-12 in ELA and mathematics; Michigan's State Board of Education unanimously adopted the standards on June 15, 2010. Rationale cited: disparate standards across states, student mobility, global competition, and changed job skills. Momentum: 48 states, the District of Columbia, and two territories supported initial development (all states but Alaska and Texas), and 35 states including Michigan had officially adopted the standards as of September 1, 2010. Development process: career and college readiness standards developed in the summer of 2009 by national experts, then K-12 learning progressions, with multiple rounds of feedback from states, associations, teachers, and the public before the June 2010 completion. Criteria: fewer, clearer, and higher; aligned with college and work expectations; rigorous content and application of knowledge through high-order skills; building on current state standards; internationally benchmarked; evidence- and research-based. The ELA standards cover Reading Literature, Reading Informational Text, Writing, Speaking, and Listening, with separate Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies and Science for grades 6-12. Mathematics standards build a K-5 foundation, extend through geometry, algebra, probability and statistics in the middle grades, and emphasize mathematical modeling in high school. A first draft of College and Career Ready Standards for Science has been developed and Social Studies standards may follow; state assessments will change, with two assessment consortiums developing multi-state assessments and Fall 2014 the current target date. District work reported: high school English language arts and middle school teachers used early versions of the Common Core as criteria for selecting new materials the board adopted last year; high school English curriculum was developed and is under revision; middle school ELA curriculum is scheduled for development this year with implementation next year; secondary math teachers explored the Common Core mathematical practices during September vertical team meetings; comparison of math common core with high school content expectations is underway pending word on course requirement changes; alignment with elementary curriculum is being evaluated; staff attended county and state Common Core rollouts; Atlas Rubicon is now used for storage and sharing of curriculum documents; the district is partnering with Oakland Schools in the Common Core Standards Initiative; and commitments include formative assessment, professional development based on evidence-based practice, parent involvement, and enhanced opportunities for Title 1 staff members.

CURRICULUM — CONSIDERATION: SEX EDUCATION ADVISORY BOARD, 2010/2011. Districts must establish a sex education advisory board; at least one-half of the board must be parents and one of the parents must co-chair. The proposed resolution approves the attached membership list. Co-chairs are Larry Hahn and Kevin Wilson. Clergy: Rev. Jack Mannschreck, Big Beaver United Methodist Church, 3753 John R Rd., Troy 48083. Health resource: Lois Winer, Nurse, Oakland Health Department, 1200 N. Resident member: Diane Trombley. Student members: Samantha Dane (AHS, 2011), Devon Gac (AHS, 2011), Lynsey Mukomel (THS, 2011), and John Biegen (THS, 2011). BUSINESS — REPORT: LEGISLATIVE UPDATE, presented October 5, 2010 by Mark Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, on State of Michigan budget adoption. School funding: in July 2010, SB 1163 passed and was signed by the Governor, setting the FY 10-11 per pupil decrease at ($154) per student. In September 2010, HB 5872, which appropriates the Federal Education Jobs Fund money, was before the Governor for signature, with three possible outcomes. Option 1, the Governor signs: HB 5872 would restore the ($154) per pupil cut for FY 10-11, with funding for TSD of $2.13 million or $177/pp as a one-time payment. Option 2, the Governor vetoes: legal speculation as to what funding formula would or could be used to distribute Federal Education Jobs money; the Governor wanted the funding formula to be solely on a 2x basis, under which Troy would receive $1.33 million, with an outside possibility the formula would be based on the Title 1 formula, under which TSD would receive $141,268. Option 3, the Governor does nothing for 14 days: the bill takes effect as passed by the House, with funding for TSD of $2.13 million.

OFFICE OF RETIREMENT SERVICES (ORS) EMPLOYER CONTRIBUTION RATE. The district received a notification letter dated February 12, 2010 of a rate change effective 10/1/2010: the employer contribution rate due on wages paid between October 1, 2010 and September 30, 2011 will be 19.41%, a 2.47% increase from the fiscal year 2010 rate of 16.94%, composed of Pension Normal Cost 3.74%, Pension Unfunded Accrued Liability 8.42%, Pension Total 12.16%, and Health Benefits (Cash Basis) 7.25%. A new notification letter dated September 29, 2010 announced rate changes effective 10/1/2010: effective October 1st the employer contribution rate for all employees except Pension Plus members is 19.41% as communicated in February, while for Pension Plus members the employer contribution rate is 17.91%. The employer contribution rate will change again for wages paid between November 1, 2010 and September 30, 2011 due to the increased number of retirees associated with the early retirement incentive: members who first worked prior to July 1, 2010 at 20.66%, and Pension Plus members at 19.16%. This rate is approximately 3 percent higher than it would be without the Preliminary Injunction, which prevents the use of employee contributions, ordered by the Court of Claims in the McMillan et al v. MPSERS et al lawsuit; at such time as the injunction may be lifted, the contribution rate will be reduced. A comparison table shows FY 2010 versus FY 2011: Normal Cost 3.98% and 3.74%; UAL 6.15% and 8.42%; Total Pension 10.13% and 12.16%; Health 6.81% and 7.25%; Total Health and Pension 16.94%, 19.41%, and Revised FY 2011 of 20.66%. The presentation notes an increased school employer rate of 1.25%, a TSD cost increase of approximately $600,000, equating to a ($50) per pupil decrease to TSD. Summary slide: one-time funding restoration under HB5872 of $177/pp, increase in ORS employer rate of -$50/pp, FY 10-11 net $127/pp, with the footnote that this only restores the district's per-pupil funding to roughly 08-09 funding levels. No action was required on the report.

OTHER. Consideration to adopt a resolution canceling the November 2, 2010, Board of Education meeting.

CLOSED SESSION. Consideration of a resolution that, as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), the Troy Board of Education go into closed session to discuss negotiations, by roll call vote of Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Pochodylo, Underwood, and Edmunds, after which no additional business would take place other than to officially adjourn.
